rules.title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act, AB 1482)
rules.requirement: In a covered unit, your landlord cannot raise your rent by more than 5% plus the local cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and can raise it at most twice in 12 months. When a new tenancy starts, the landlord can set any starting rent, and the cap applies to increases after that.
rules.key_value: Lower of 5% + regional CPI or 10% per 12 months; at most 2 increases per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property in California, including mobilehome park units. It applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (February 18, 2021 for mobilehome tenancies). It does not cover housing that received its certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (rolling test), unless it is a mobilehome. It does not apply where a local rent control ordinance limits increases below this cap, such as the Los Angeles RSO. The section is set to be repealed on January 1, 2030.
rules.exemptions: Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years. Deed-restricted, regulatory-restricted or subsidized affordable housing. School and university dormitories. Housing under local rent control that limits increases below this cap. Separately alienable units, such as single-family homes and condos, when the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member and the tenant got the required written notice. Owner-occupied duplexes where the owner has lived in one unit since the start of the tenancy and neither unit is an ADU or JADU. Mobilehome homeowners.
rules.penalty: The tenant can sue for injunctive relief, damages equal to the overcharge, and discretionary attorney's fees and costs. The tenant can recover up to three times the overcharge for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct. The Attorney General and the city attorney or county counsel may also enforce. The statute of limitations is three years, and waivers are void.

exemption_tests.description: Housing that received its certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (rolling test)
Owner-occupied duplex where the owner has lived in one unit since the start of the tenancy and neither unit is an ADU or JADU
Separately alienable single-family home or condo not owned by a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant received the required written exemption notice

rules.conflict_note: AB 1482 was originally effective January 1, 2020. The current version (SB 567) took effect January 1, 2024 and became operative April 1, 2024. That is an amendment, not a conflict between sources. The annual maximum percentages cited on one page (8.9% for Aug 2024–Jul 2025) are outdated, so check the current figure.
rules.reason: All four candidates describe Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12, so they were merged into one record citing the statute text; the effective date is set to AB 1482's original 2020 date rather than the SB 567 operative date.
